holidays.name: National Take a Hike Day
holidays.description: A day encouraging everyone to lace up their boots, step away from the couch, and hit a trail. Whether it's a mountain path or a stroll around the neighborhood, the goal is to get outside and move.
holidays.origin: Created by the American Hiking Society in 2015 to promote hiking and the preservation of trails across the United States.
holidays.funFact: Hiking is such a beloved pastime that the Appalachian Trail, spanning about 2,190 miles, is hiked end-to-end by only a few thousand people each year, and many more try and give up.

holidays.name: National Homemade Bread Day
holidays.description: A carb-lover's dream, this day celebrates the art of baking bread from scratch, from crusty sourdough loaves to soft dinner rolls. Flour-covered counters and warm, yeasty kitchens are strongly encouraged.
holidays.origin: An unofficial food observance popularized by baking enthusiasts and food calendars, celebrating one of humanity's oldest prepared foods.
holidays.funFact: Archaeologists have found evidence of bread-like food made over 14,000 years ago, which means people were baking before they were farming.

holidays.name: Unfriend Day
holidays.description: A tongue-in-cheek day for cleaning up your social media friend list by removing people you barely know, no longer talk to, or who just post too many vague status updates.
holidays.origin: Launched in 2010 by comedian Jimmy Kimmel as a joke on his late night show, urging viewers to unfriend people on Facebook. It quickly became a recurring internet observance.
holidays.funFact: The word 'unfriend' was named the New Oxford American Dictionary's Word of the Year in 2009, just before this day came along.

holidays.name: International Students Day
holidays.description: A day honoring students around the world and their ongoing struggle for education, rights, and academic freedom. Part celebration, part call to action.
holidays.origin: Established in 1941 in London to commemorate the Nazi suppression of Czech universities and the students who protested on November 17, 1939. It's now observed by many countries.
holidays.funFact: In the Czech Republic, November 17 is also a public holiday called Struggle for Freedom and Democracy Day, linked to the 1989 Velvet Revolution.

holidays.name: World Prematurity Day
holidays.description: An awareness day highlighting the challenges of premature birth and the need for better care for preemies and their families. Landmarks around the world light up in purple.
holidays.origin: Started by European parent organizations in 2008, it grew into a global observance supported by many health organizations and hospitals.
holidays.funFact: Roughly 1 in 10 babies worldwide is born prematurely, and purple is the signature color of the awareness campaign.
